exercises.instruction: In Exercises 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, find the derivative $$dy \slash dx$$ (a) by solving each of the implicit equations for $$y$$ explicitly in terms of $$x$$ and (b) by differentiating each of the equations implicitly. Show that in each case, the results are equivalent.

problem.paragraph: Volume of a Cylinder The volume of a right-circular cylinder of radius $$r$$ and height $$h$$ is $$V = \pi r^{2}h$$ . Suppose the radius and height of the cylinder are changing with respect to time $$t$$ .

list.item: Find a relationship between $$dV \slash dt$$ , $$dr \slash dt$$ , and $$dh \slash dt$$ .

At a certain instant of time, the radius and height of the cylinder are $$2$$ and $$6$$ in. and are increasing at the rate of $$0.1{in.} \slash \sec$$ and $$0.3{in.} \slash \sec$$ , respectively. How fast is the volume of the cylinder increasing?

problem.paragraph: Distance Between Two Cars A car leaves an intersection traveling west. Its position $$4$$ sec later is $$20$$ ft from the intersection. At the same time, another car leaves the same intersection heading north so that its position $$4$$ sec later is $$28$$ ft from the intersection. If the speeds of the cars at that instant of time are $$9{ft} \slash \sec$$ and $$11{ft} \slash \sec$$ , respectively, find the rate at which the distance between the two cars is changing.

where $$p$$ is measured in dollars and $$x$$ is measured in units of a thousand. How fast is the quantity demanded weekly changing when $$x = 9$$ , $$p = 63$$ , and the price per tire is increasing at the rate of $$\$ 2 \slash {week}$$ ?
Effect of Price on Supply of Tires Suppose the quantity $$x$$ of Super Titan radial tires made available each week in the marketplace is related to the unit selling price by the equation

where $$x$$ is measured in units of a thousand and $$p$$ is in dollars. How fast is the weekly supply of Super Titan radial tires being introduced into the marketplace changing when $$x = 6$$ , $$p = 66$$ , and the price per tire is decreasing at the rate of $$\$ 3 \slash {week}$$ ?
Effect of Price on Demand for Headphones The demand equation for a certain brand of two-way headphones is

where $$x$$ represents the number (in thousands) of headphones demanded each week when the unit price is $$\$ p$$ . How fast is the quantity demanded increasing when the unit price per headphone is $$\$ 14$$ and the price is dropping at the rate of $$\$ 0.15 \slash {headphone} \slash {week}$$ ?
Hint: To find the value of $$x$$ when $$p = 14$$ , solve the equation $$100x^{2} + 9p^{2} = 3600$$ for $$x$$ when $$p = 14$$ .

Effect of Price on Supply of Eggs Suppose the wholesale price of a certain brand of medium-sized eggs $$p$$ (in dollars per carton) is related to the weekly supply $$x$$ (in thousands of cartons) by the equation

If $$25,000$$ cartons of eggs are available at the beginning of a certain week and the price is falling at the rate of $$2¢ \slash {carton} \slash {week}$$ , at what rate is the weekly supply falling?
Hint: To find the value of $$p$$ when $$x = 25$$ , solve the supply equation for $$p$$ when $$x = 25$$ .

Effect of Supply on Price of Eggs Refer to Exercise 44. If $$25,000$$ cartons of eggs are available at the beginning of a certain week and the weekly supply is falling at the rate of $$1000{cartons} \slash {week}$$ , at what rate is the wholesale price changing?

where $$p$$ is the unit price in dollars and $$x$$ is the quantity demanded each week, measured in units of a thousand. Compute the elasticity of demand and determine whether the demand is inelastic, unitary, or elastic when $$x = 10$$ .
Elasticity of Demand for CDs The demand function for a certain brand of compact disc is

where $$p$$ is the wholesale unit price in dollars and $$x$$ is the quantity demanded each week, measured in units of a thousand. Compute the elasticity of demand and determine whether the demand is inelastic, unitary, or elastic when $$x = 15$$ .
Production Function for a Furniture Company The manager of Dixie Furniture Company estimates that the daily output of her factory (in thousands of dollars) $$Q$$ is given by
where $$x$$ is the amount spent on labor and $$y$$ is the amount spent on capital (both measured in thousands of dollars).

list.item: Find the daily output of the factory if $$\$ 16,000$$ is spent on labor and $$\$ 81,000$$ is spent on capital each day.

Suppose that the output of the factory is to be maintained at the level found in part (a). By how much should the amount spent on capital be changed if the amount on labor is increased by $$\$ 1000$$ ? What is the MRTS?

problem.paragraph: Output of a Country Suppose that the output $$Q$$ of a certain country is given by $$Q = 20x^{3 \slash 5}y^{2 \slash 5}$$ billion dollars if $$x$$ billion dollars are spent on labor and $$y$$ billion dollars are spent on capital.

list.item: Find the output of the country if it spends $$\$ 32$$ billion on labor and $$\$ 243$$ billion on capital.

Suppose that the output of the country is to be maintained at the level found in part (a). By how much should the amount spent on capital be changed if the amount spent on labor is increased by $$\$ 1$$ billion? What is the MRTS?

problem.paragraph: Volume of a Cube The volume $$V$$ of a cube with sides of length $$x$$ in. is changing with respect to time. At a certain instant of time, the sides of the cube are $$5$$ in. long and increasing at the rate of $$0.1{in.} \slash \sec$$ . How fast is the volume of the cube changing at that instant of time?

Oil Spills In calm waters, the oil spilling from the ruptured hull of a grounded tanker spreads in all directions. Assuming that the area polluted is circular, determine how fast the area is increasing when the radius of the circle is $$60$$ ft and is increasing at the rate of $$\frac{1}{2}{ft} \slash \sec$$ ?

Distance Between Two Ships Two ships leave the same port at noon. Ship $$A$$ sails north at $$15$$ mph, and Ship $$B$$ sails east at $$12$$ mph. How fast is the distance between them changing at 1 p.m.?

Oil Spills In calm waters, the oil spilling from the ruptured hull of a grounded tanker spreads in all directions. Assuming that the area polluted is circular, determine how fast the radius of the circle is changing when the area of the circle is $$1600\pi{ft}^{2}$$ and increasing at the rate of $$80\pi{ft}^{2} \slash \sec$$ .

Distance Between Two Cars A car leaves an intersection traveling east. Its position $$t$$ sec later is given by $$x = t^{2} + t$$ ft. At the same time, another car leaves the same intersection heading north, traveling $$y = t^{2} + 3t$$ ft in $$t$$ sec. Find the rate at which the distance between the two cars will be changing $$5$$ sec later.

Distance Between Two Cars A car leaves an intersection traveling west. Its position $$4$$ sec later is $$20$$ ft from the intersection. At the same time, another car leaves the same intersection heading north so that its position $$t$$ sec later is $$t^{2} + 2t$$ ft from the intersection. If the speed of the first car $$4$$ sec after leaving the intersection is $$9{ft} \slash \sec$$ , find the rate at which the distance between the two cars is changing at that instant of time.

Watching a Helicopter Take Off At a distance of $$50$$ ft from the pad, a man observes a helicopter taking off from a heliport. If the helicopter lifts off vertically and is rising at a speed of $$44{ft} \slash \sec$$ when it is at an altitude of $$120$$ ft, how fast is the distance between the helicopter and the man changing at that instant?

Watching a Rowing Race A spectator watches a rowing race from the edge of a river bank. The lead boat is moving in a straight line that is $$120$$ ft from the river bank. If the boat is moving at a constant speed of $$20{ft} \slash \sec$$ , how fast is the boat moving away from the spectator when it is $$50$$ ft past her?

Docking a Boat A boat is pulled toward a dock by means of a rope wound on a drum that is located $$4$$ ft above the bow of the boat. If the rope is being pulled in at the rate of $$3{ft} \slash \sec$$ , how fast is the boat approaching the dock when it is $$25$$ ft from the dock?

image.alt: Details An illustration shows a boat tied to a cylindrical drum on a dock by means of a rope. One end of the rope is tied to the boat’s bow and the other end is wound around the drum.

problem.paragraph: A Melting Snowball Assume that a snowball is in the shape of a sphere. If the snowball melts at a rate that is proportional to its surface area, show that its radius decreases at a constant rate.
Hint: Its volume is $$V = (4 \slash 3)\pi r^{3}$$ , and its surface area is $$S = 4\pi r^{2}$$ .

Blowing Soap Bubbles Carlos is blowing air into a soap bubble at the rate of $$8{cm}^{3} \slash \sec$$ . Assuming that the bubble is spherical, how fast is its radius changing at the instant of time when the radius is $$10$$ cm? How fast is the surface area of the bubble changing at that instant of time?

Coast Guard Patrol Search Mission The pilot of a Coast Guard patrol aircraft on a search mission had just spotted a disabled fishing trawler and decided to go in for a closer look. Flying in a straight line at a constant altitude of $$1000$$ ft and at a steady speed of $$264{ft} \slash \sec$$ , the aircraft passed directly over the trawler. How fast was the aircraft receding from the trawler when it was $$1500$$ ft from the trawler?

image.alt: Details An illustration shows a fishing trawler located on a horizontal line and a patrol aircraft moving ahead of it along a horizontal line above. The vertical, direct distance between the two lines is 1000 feet. A straight line sloping upward to the right connects the trawler and the aircraft.

problem.paragraph: Filling a Coffee Pot A coffee pot in the form of a circular cylinder of radius $$4$$ in. is being filled with water flowing at a constant rate. If the water level is rising at the rate of $$0.4{in.} \slash \sec$$ , what is the rate at which water is flowing into the coffee pot?

image.alt: An illustration shows a glass coffee mug filled with water to a height of h units from the bottom.

problem.paragraph: Movement of a Shadow A $$6$$ -ft tall man is walking away from a street light $$18$$ ft high at a speed of $$6{ft} \slash \sec$$ . How fast is the tip of his shadow moving along the ground?

A Sliding Ladder A $$20$$ -ft ladder leaning against a wall begins to slide. How fast is the top of the ladder sliding down the wall at the instant of time when the bottom of the ladder is $$12$$ ft from the wall and sliding away from the wall at the rate of $$5{ft} \slash \sec$$ ?
Hint: Refer to the accompanying figure. By the Pythagorean Theorem, $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 400$$ . Find $$dy \slash dt$$ when $$x = 12$$ and $$dx \slash dt = 5$$ .

An arrow at the foot of the ladder pointing away from the wall is labeled 5 feet per second.

problem.paragraph: A Sliding Ladder The base of a $$13$$ -ft ladder leaning against a wall begins to slide away from the wall. At the instant of time when the base is $$12$$ ft from the wall, the base is moving at the rate of $$8{ft} \slash \sec$$ . How fast is the top of the ladder sliding down the wall at that instant of time?
Hint: Refer to the hint in Problem 64.

How fast was the height of the water decreasing when its height was $$8$$ ft?

Volume of a Gas In an adiabatic process (one in which no heat transfer takes place), the pressure $$P$$ and volume $$V$$ of an ideal gas such as oxygen satisfy the equation $$P^{5}V^{7} = C$$ , where $$C$$ is a constant. Suppose that at a certain instant of time, the volume of the gas is $$4$$ L, the pressure is $$100$$ kPa, and the pressure is decreasing at the rate of $$5{kPa} \slash \sec$$ . Find the rate at which the volume is changing.
